parts.text: Which labelling of shape to function is correct?

options.text: Thin flat sheet: protective lining; long branched thread: carrying messages; spindle: contracting to help move food.
Long branched thread: protective lining; thin flat sheet: carrying messages; spindle: contracting to help move food.
All three models must share one shape because they come from the same person.
The long branched thread moves food down the food pipe because it is long like the pipe.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Aditya shapes three clay models for a class display: a thin flat sheet that can cover a surface, a long thread with side branches, and a short spindle that can shorten when squeezed. He labels them as models of a cheek cell, a nerve cell, and a food-pipe muscle cell.

part_answers.answer: Each cell's shape and structure match its job: flat lining, long branched message paths, and spindles that contract.

teacher.key_rationale: Cell shape and structure support function: flat cheek cells line surfaces, long branched nerve cells carry messages, and spindle muscle cells contract. Swapping labels or treating all cells alike misses that link.
